# Topic index {#sec-appf}

Use this alphabetical index when you know a topic but not where the book discusses it. An entry gives the
destination's title and a section reference or link. Read that destination to decide whether it answers your
question; an index hit alone is not evidence that the topic is fully explained.

To follow an entry:

1. Look for the topic in alphabetical order, including any qualifier after a comma. A qualifier narrows what
   the entry covers: "symbols, diffusion" concerns notation, rather than every question about diffusion.
2. If the entry says "see", continue to the named index term. For example, "symbol table" redirects to
   "notation index"; it does not name a second destination.
3. Follow the destination reference or link, then read the section itself. If an entry lists several
   destinations, use their titles to distinguish their scope rather than assuming each answers the same question.
4. Check whether the destination supplies the definition, assumptions or procedure you need. A heading with
   no explanation does not establish an answer, even when its link resolves.

The entries below currently lead to the notation index and its subject groups. Those groups organise symbols;
their titles do not promise a derivation or an implementation guide. In particular, "symbols, diffusion" is a
notation destination. The source does contain `diffusion_tendency`, which calls `diffusion_coefficients`
({{< code src/diffusion/diffusion.cpp diffusion_tendency >}}). This source fact does not turn a notation-group
entry into an explanation of the diffusion method.

Absence from this index is also not evidence that the code lacks a feature. Keep the questions separate:
whether an entry exists, whether its destination answers the question, and whether the implementation supports
the requested operation. A source citation can establish a code fact without establishing that a book route is
complete. The code example above is source reading, not runtime validation.

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Not provided: comprehensive topic coverage or verified answers for every indexed heading, because the current
entries point to the notation index and its subject groups. Missing mechanism-specific entries and incomplete
destinations remain gaps in the book's navigation and content; they are not declarations of unsupported code.
:::
